# Shed Industries

> Shed Industries is a UK brand strategy consultancy helping growing businesses get clear on their brand, their market, and their path forward. Founded by Mark McAulay, who brings twenty years of design agency experience and six years as a founder building a brand in the food and drink sector from the ground up.

Shed Industries works with businesses on four things that determine whether a brand competes or gets left behind: market research, competitor analysis, messaging, and brand roadmap. The consultancy is built for growing businesses whose brand hasn't kept pace with their growth — the moment worked at an earlier stage but is losing its edge in a larger, sharper market.

## Services

- [Market Research](https://shed.io/brand-strategy/market-research/): Evidence-based research into who the customers are, what they value, and how their expectations are shifting.
- [Competitor Analysis](https://shed.io/brand-strategy/competitor-analysis/): Mapping how competitors are positioned, where they are vulnerable, and what space is available to own.
- [Messaging](https://shed.io/brand-strategy/messaging/): Defining what a business says, how it says it, and to whom — the narrative a brand carries into every market and conversation.
- [Brand Roadmap](https://shed.io/brand-strategy/brand-roadmap/): A clear, prioritised plan for what changes, what stays, what gets built, and in what order.
- [Brand Strategy](https://shed.io/brand-strategy/): Plain definitions of what brand strategy is, where it sits in a business, when a business needs it, and how it differs from creative direction, plus an FAQ.

## Journal

Honest thinking on brand positioning, market dynamics, and messaging, published when it's worth reading.

- [Journal index](https://shed.io/journal/): All articles.
- ["Brand" Is Doing Too Much Work](https://shed.io/journal/brand-is-doing-too-much-work/): Why brand strategy keeps getting mistaken for design, marketing and creative direction, with examples of it working, failing, and what five leading agencies do differently.
- [Good Is Everywhere Now. Ideas Aren't.](https://shed.io/journal/good-is-everywhere-ideas-arent/): AI has raised the baseline of good work for everyone, fast — but it can't have the idea in the first place, and that's still where businesses stand out.
- [I Don't Trust AI That Agrees With Me](https://shed.io/journal/i-dont-trust-ai-that-agrees-with-me/): Almost a year building a consultancy with Claude as a working partner, and why an AI that only agrees isn't saving time — it's quietly making judgement worse.
- [The Blast-Beat Guide to Brand Strategy](https://shed.io/journal/the-blast-beat-guide-to-brand-strategy/): What Napalm Death and Dolly Parton have in common, and what it means for building a brand that lasts.
- [The Comfortable Danger Zone](https://shed.io/journal/the-comfortable-danger-zone/): What settled success can hide, and how to see vulnerability before it becomes a problem.
- [What a Brand Roadmap Actually Is](https://shed.io/journal/what-a-brand-roadmap-actually-is/): Why a roadmap is a prioritised plan, not a vision statement.
